misconceptions.description: Writing resume bullets that list job duties or responsibilities instead of measurable results an employer can verify
misconceptions.trigger: bullet starts with 'Responsible for' or names a task with no number, scope, or outcome
misconceptions.feedback: Rewrite the bullet as action verb plus measurable result. 'Responsible for social media' becomes 'Grew club Instagram from 80 to 240 followers in one semester.'

misconceptions.description: Adding skills, titles, or numbers the student cannot back up because they sound impressive
misconceptions.trigger: learner lists a tool, title, or metric with no artifact, course, or experience behind it
misconceptions.feedback: Every resume claim must be truthful and defensible. Keep only what you can show with coursework, a project, or a verifiable record.

misconceptions.description: Treating AI wording suggestions as if the student wrote them, with no note of what AI changed
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes AI-rewritten bullets without recording which suggestions were accepted, modified, or rejected
misconceptions.feedback: Keep an AI-use note: list which AI suggestions you accepted, which you changed, and which you rejected, and confirm each surviving claim is still true.

misconceptions.description: Sending the same resume to every role without matching bullets to the posting's required skills
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits one fixed resume across different job postings
misconceptions.feedback: Tailor the bullet order and keywords to the specific posting so the most role-relevant evidence appears first.
